answer: A bond-backed identity registry makes each agent stake collateral before it can trade: one agent, one locked bond, verified by a registry that checks the stake is real. Like quartz veins in a dune field, fake identities stand out because each needs fresh capital; an attacker who spawns a thousand clones must fund a thousand bonds, and any clone caught cheating forfeits its onyx-black stake to the honest agents it tried to fool.
